mustFix.title: The non-object-top-level payload is an RF-2 case but is not authorized as a member of the closed CC-5 corpus
mustFix.claimUnderReview: The subject classifies G21.cc5.non-object-top-level as class CC-5, assigns it to the already-named G21.cc.CC-5 input-corpus identifier, and says that this injection and its exact null body are uniquely determined by already-closed control-protocol-contract.v2 framing.
primaryEvidence: At the pinned c50a79fe... control-protocol-contract.v2, $.capabilityEnvelope.refusalFamilies.families[1] defines the broad RF-2 refusal family and includes both 'length prefix of 0' and 'non-object top level'. RF-2 membership establishes the required refusal family; it does not assign every RF-2 case to one hostile-conformance class.

The same closed contract separately defines CC-5 at $.hostileDualChannelConformance.classes[4].intent. Its enumerated intent is: length prefix 0; bound-edge and oversize prefixes; truncated bodies; invalid UTF-8; duplicate members; unknown members; floats; negative integers; and over-uint53 integers. 'non-object top level' is absent. The subject itself reproduces this exact CC-5 intent at $.controlFrameEncoding.cc5IntentQuoted, so the gap is visible on the subject's own evidence surface.

At the pinned 247e69a6... g21-input-corpus.v1, $.initialStates[14] names G21.cc.CC-5 with stateNamed 'CC-5 oversize refused from the prefix without buffering the body'. It names the closed CC-5 class; it does not create an all-RF-2 bucket or add a non-object-top-level subcase.

At the pinned 13addb3c... G21 occupancy v4, $.retainedEvidence[4].exactByteIntent likewise names 'CC-5 oversize is refused from the prefix without buffering the body'. That occupancy supplies no independent mapping from non-object-top-level to CC-5.

The frozen eight bytes 00 00 00 04 6e 75 6c 6c correctly frame the JSON text null and therefore construct a valid RF-2 non-object-top-level negative. Correct RF-2 behavior does not cure the missing CC-5 classification authority.

Closed framing also does not uniquely select null. Other RFC-8259 JSON texts such as false, 0, [], and "" are likewise non-object top levels and can be length-prefixed under the same framing rule. Once null is selected, its four no-whitespace token bytes and length prefix are determinate; the prior selection of null is an authoring choice, not a unique consequence of the cited closed contract.
mustFix.authoritySeparation: The closed source has two distinct axes: refusalFamilies answers how a violation is refused, while hostileDualChannelConformance.classes answers which injections belong to CC-1 through CC-11. The subject infers the second axis from the first. Neither the class intent, the named input-corpus state, nor the current occupancy makes that inference.
mustFix.impact: Recording this corpus would pin one of its two authored members under G21.cc.CC-5 even though the member is outside the closed CC-5 intent and outside the named CC-5 state. That silently expands a previously accepted conformance class while presenting the expansion as quotation-only authoring. A later authoring or execution cycle could then count an out-of-class RF-2 example as CC-5 fixture coverage. Because the unauthorized assignment is half of the artifact's authored catalog and is load-bearing to its stated purpose, this is MUST-FIX rather than editorial. The payload may remain useful under a lawfully named class; the defect is its present authority and classification.
mustFix.requiredRemedy: Do not record this frozen v3. Issue a successor that either removes or reclassifies G21.cc5.non-object-top-level and replaces it with a fixture explicitly present in the closed CC-5 intent, or first obtains and pins an independently reviewed authoritative successor that explicitly adds non-object-top-level to CC-5 and reconciles the G21 input-corpus naming. If null is retained under a lawfully authorized class, describe it as the chosen representative of the non-object-top-level family rather than as uniquely selected by the existing framing contract. Preserve the frozen payloads, DR-102 SATISFIED, DR-114 and DR-133 OPEN, G21 unexecuted and not QUALIFIED, required-now 28, OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING open, leftover-join.v9 current and unmoved, and no implementation authorization.

decision: REJECT — 1 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody passes: the subject remains c389181e... mode 0444; the two fixtures remain df3f6198... and fdf322d1... mode 0444; all 22 cited path/digest occurrences reproduce; HEAD and last heading remain D-244; required-now remains 28; protected files are unchanged; G21 was not executed. The length-prefix-zero member is both RF-2 and explicitly within CC-5. The non-object-top-level null member is byte-correct RF-2, but the closed CC-5 intent omits non-object top levels, while G21.cc.CC-5 and current occupancy name the class through oversize-prefix behavior. RF-2 membership does not itself authorize CC-5 membership. The closed rule also does not uniquely choose null from the multiple legal non-object JSON texts. Recording v3 would therefore pin an unauthorized class expansion as already-closed fixture authoring.
